title: 1955 AHSME Problem 46
statement: The graphs of \(2x+3y-6=0,\) \(4x-3y-6=0,\) \(x=2,\) and \(y=\dfrac23\) intersect in:

solutions.text:
Adding the first two equations gives \(6x-12=0,\) so \(x=2.\) Substitution gives \(3y=2,\) hence \(y=\frac{2}{3}.\) This point also lies on the last two given lines. Therefore all four graphs have the single common point \((2,\frac{2}{3}).\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Solve the first two linear equations simultaneously
Check whether that solution also satisfies each of the last two displayed equations
